core_obligations: Choose the nonzero element supplied by auto-associatedness and note that a power of every element of the maximal ideal kills it (proof lines 3699-3700).

Write the given proper ideal by finitely many generators and show that the chosen element lies in the kernel of the map to the product of the localisations at those generators (proof lines 3700-3703).
Apply the covering criterion to obtain a nonzero element annihilated by each generator, which is the asserted property (P) (proof lines 3703-3705).
proof_roadmap: Place it in the kernel of the covering map (proof lines 3700-3703).
difficulty_reason: The lemma derives the annihilator property (P) from auto-associatedness, and the proof is a 7-line argument that produces the annihilator explicitly. From the defining element of an auto-associated ring, which is killed by a power of every element of the maximal ideal, it deduces that this element lies in the kernel of the map to the product of the localisations at the generators of the given ideal, and then applies a criterion of the Algebra chapter which turns that membership into a nonzero annihilator of the whole ideal. The two steps — the production of the element and the covering criterion — are each a single displayed computation.
